APP (Atactic Polypropylene) Modified Bitumen Waterproofing Membrane

APP (Atactic Polypropylene) modified bitumen membrane is a reinforced waterproofing sheet where the bitumen is modified with a plastomeric polymer. This modification gives the membrane superior heat resistance — up to 130°C for Type II grades — making it the product of choice for hot-climate roofing and exposed roof systems. It is typically installed by torch application (hot-melt), though cold-bonding methods are also compatible.

APP is often shortlisted for high-temperature stability.

APP is the preferred specification for hot-climate regions (Middle East, Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia) where roof surface temperatures regularly exceed 70°C. APP's plastomeric modification provides dimensional stability at high temperatures that SBS (rubber-modified) cannot match. Conversely, SBS excels in cold climates with low-temperature flexibility down to -25°C. If your project is in a hot region with high solar exposure, APP is the right choice.

APP modification fundamentally changes the bitumen's molecular structure, making it highly resistant to oxidation and the brittle failure typically caused by long-term UV exposure in tropical environments.

EPDM (Ethylene-Propylene Diene Monomer) is a cured rubber membrane used where flexible sheet performance and weathering resistance are the deciding factors: exposed roofing, bridge decks, water infrastructure, and buried applications. Vulcanized EPDM has rubber memory — it wants to spring back. Rolls are wound on rigid cardboard cores under controlled tension and held with PE film so they arrive round, not oval, and unroll flat on site.

Vulcanized EPDM is cross-linked during production, delivering higher mechanical performance — tensile strength ≥ 7.5 MPa, elongation ≥ 450%, tear strength ≥ 25 kN/m — and better low-temperature flexibility. Non-vulcanized grades (tensile ≥ 4.0 MPa, elongation ≥ 400%) are easier to bond and shape around complex details, at slightly lower strength. Select the type based on the mechanical demand of the project; vulcanized is the standard for exposed roofing.

Vulcanized EPDM stretches past 450% and returns to shape, absorbing thermal cycling, structural settlement, and substrate cracking without stress concentration. Rigid membranes transfer that movement to the seam line; EPDM absorbs it in the sheet itself.
